title: Composition of derived direct images for ringed spaces
statement: Let $f:(X,\mathcal O_X)\to(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ and $g:(Y,\mathcal O_Y)\to(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$ be morphisms of ringed spaces [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism], and let $Rf_*$, $Rg_*$, $R(g\circ f)_*$ be the derived direct images on the derived categories of sheaves of modules [def-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image]. There is a canonical isomorphism $Rg_*\circ Rf_*\cong R(g\circ f)_*$ of functors $D(\mathcal O_X)\to D(\mathcal O_Z)$.

proof.text: The ringed-space derived adjunction statement [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-adjoint-general] gives adjunctions $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$, $Lg^*\dashv Rg_*$, and $L(g\circ f)^*\dashv R(g\circ f)_*$ on the corresponding derived categories.

The derived pullback composition statement [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-pullback-composition] supplies a canonical natural isomorphism $Lf^*\circ Lg^*\cong L(g\circ f)^*$, so transporting the last adjunction across this isomorphism makes $R(g\circ f)_*$ a right adjoint of $Lf^*\circ Lg^*$.

Apply [lem-cat-right-adjoint-composition] with $F=Lg^*$, $G=Lf^*$, $F^!=Rg_*$, $G^!=Rf_*$, and $(G\circ F)^!=R(g\circ f)_*$. It gives a canonical natural isomorphism $R(g\circ f)_*\cong Rg_*\circ Rf_*$. Taking its inverse yields the required canonical isomorphism $Rg_*\circ Rf_*\cong R(g\circ f)_*$, natural as an isomorphism of functors $D(\mathcal O_X)\to D(\mathcal O_Z)$.
